ca_sub_summit.blurb: Sub-Summit is a hillside of boulders and short walls at Lake Ramona in north San Diego County, sitting above the main boulder rows and east of the summit zone. Most of the climbing is bouldering, from VB up to the double digits, with a smaller set of short trad leads and a single top rope. The Arkenstone (V2) is the standout problem here. Shade is scarce in the middle of the day and the slope is dry and warm, so mornings and late afternoons are the comfortable windows. The ground is brushy and uneven, so bring pads and watch your landings.
ca_sub_summit.parking_note: The walk begins at the Blue Sky Ecological Reserve lot, then follows the trail up toward the Lake Ramona dam and the boulder-covered slopes beyond it.
ca_sub_summit.approach: Rather than cutting straight up through the boulders below, swing around and come onto the hillside from the west side.

ca_sunshine_face_right_side.blurb: The right side of the Sunshine Face is a steep, exposed stretch of granite slab and crack climbing on Suicide Rock above Idyllwild. Nearly everything is trad, with a few top ropes, and the grades cluster in the 5.11 and 5.12 range with a handful of easier lines. Protection can be sparse and face climbs are often runout, so it suits confident leaders. Valhalla, Moondance, Sundance, Hesitation and Ishi are among the best known. The face gets shade early in the day, which helps in warm weather, and pine needles can collect on lower ledges and reduce friction.
ca_sunshine_face_right_side.parking_note: Take Fern Valley Road up toward Humber Park, turn right onto Forest Drive, and leave the car near the large green water tanks.
ca_sunshine_face_right_side.approach: A climbers' trail starts opposite the tanks, drops to a seasonal stream, joins a paved lane to its end, then climbs a signed, rocky path to the base of the cliff.

ca_central_royal_arches.blurb: The Royal Arches form a long band of sweeping slabs, dihedrals and cracks on the north side of Yosemite Valley, and the central section holds the wall's most traveled climbing. Most lines are trad, with a few sport and aid routes, and the grades sit mainly in the 5.10 and 5.11 range. Texas Chainsaw Massacre is a named test piece. Expect polished rock, some route-finding and, on the longer lines, a big day out. The wall sees full sun by mid-morning, so start early in summer; in spring the gullies and upper slabs can be wet and dirty.
ca_central_royal_arches.parking_note: Park at the Church Bowl picnic area in Yosemite Valley and pick up the trail that climbs toward the base of the arches.

ca_east_wall_inner_exorcist_area.blurb: This is the inner part of the East Wall in the Hall of Horrors, a cluster of granite formations in central Joshua Tree. The west-facing side is the biggest face in the group and mixes crack climbing with face moves. Nearly all of it is trad, with a few bolted and top-rope options, and grades run from easy cracks through a good spread of 5.8 to 5.10 up to a few hard faces. Exorcist and Love Goddess are the named lines here. There is no water nearby and little shade in the heat, so start early or climb late in the day.
ca_east_wall_inner_exorcist_area.approach: From the lot, go right along the end of the East Wall, then bend left into the broad valley between the two main formations; the face rises on your left.

ca_poison_oak_boulder_area.blurb: This is a group of large granitic boulders on Mount Woodson in north San Diego County, where the rock is compact and the climbing is mostly crack, slab and technical face. A lot of it is set up as top rope, alongside trad leads, a few boulder problems and some bolted lines, and most grades fall between 5.10 and 5.12. Big Grunt, Starving In Stereo and Elsa's Crack are good places to start. Brush here is thick and poison oak is common, so wear long sleeves, expect rough trails and carry plenty of water. Summer heat can be harsh.

ca_pep_boys_crag.blurb: Pep Boys Crag is a long, low outcrop among the Roadside Rocks near Hidden Valley in Joshua Tree, with climbing at each end and little in between. It is almost entirely trad, plus a few top ropes, and the grades are friendly: plenty of 5.7 through 5.10 cracks and a scattering of easier and harder lines. It is a quick stop that suits warm-ups and short days rather than a destination wall. Sections facing the road catch morning sun, while the sides toward the neighboring formation warm up later. Sand in the cracks and sharp edges near roofs can make some pitches feel trickier than the grade.
ca_pep_boys_crag.parking_note: Use the paved pullout beside the Milepost formation on the park road; the crag lies a short stroll southeast of it.

ca_jellystone_southwest_face.blurb: Jellystone is a roadside formation in the Lost Horse area of Joshua Tree, and its southwest face holds a tidy collection of short, mostly trad climbs with a handful of top ropes and two bolted lines. The grades lean friendly, with many routes between 5.5 and 5.10 and only a few harder ones, so it works well for beginners learning to place gear and for quick laps. Protection on the thinner cracks can be sparse. The face gets afternoon sun and offers little shade, so plan for an earlier start in warm weather and bring water.

ca_olmsted_canyon_right.blurb: The right fork of Olmsted Canyon, just off Tioga Road near Tuolumne Meadows, is a secluded granite crack arena that is all trad. Grades concentrate between 5.10 and 5.12, with a few moderate lines and one very hard route, Broken Arrow. Tideline, Lord Caffeine, Ivory Tower Center and The Thrill Is Gone draw the most attention. Clean, firm granite and good gear make it a fine place to warm up before longer outings. The walls get early sun and shade later in the day. This is high country, so late spring through early fall is the realistic window.
ca_olmsted_canyon_right.parking_note: Leave the car at the small paved turnout just beyond Olmsted Point, near the mouth of the canyon.
ca_olmsted_canyon_right.approach: A marked footpath crosses forest and open meadow, heading up the canyon to the right fork.

ca_main_wall_6.blurb: The Main Wall is the big face of Tollhouse Rock, a granite dome in the Sierra foothills, with low-angle slabs, a couple of fine cracks and routes up to four pitches. Nearly everything is trad, with a few bolted lines, and most grades fall between 5.7 and 5.10, though locals consider the ratings stiff and face climbs are often runout. Tollhouse Traverse, Free and Easy, Elephant Walk, Beginner's Delight and Wandering Taoist are the favorites. Winter sun makes it a good fall-through-spring destination, but it is hot in summer.
ca_main_wall_6.parking_note: From Tollhouse Road, take Burrough Mountain Road, a rough dirt track. A pullout near the powerlines about a mile up works for ordinary cars; high-clearance vehicles can go higher toward the top of the rock.
ca_main_wall_6.approach: From the top of the road, a use trail drops down a slab gully on the east side, cuts below the bolted slab, and follows the base of the wall through manzanita.

ca_2_southwest_face.blurb: The southwest face is the broad, sunlit side of El Capitan, the 3,000-foot granite wall on the north side of Yosemite Valley, and it carries some of the most storied big-wall routes in the world. Most routes here are climbed with aid, though a few go free at high grades, and a smaller number are trad lines. The Nose, Salathe Wall, Golden Gate, Lurking Fear and Freerider are among them, and Magic Mushroom marks the very hard end. These are multi-day undertakings for experienced wall climbers, with hauling, bivouacs and long rappel descents; casual visitors can enjoy it from the meadows below.
